app.notes:
### Changed

- **The save bar shows only where it saves.** App settings keeps your choices as you change them, so the board's Revert / Save bar is gone from it; it stays on the Controller and Pico 2 W pages, whose settings it saves.
- **One Set up USB access, for the app and for games (Linux).** The same button now installs one rule that lets the app reach your board and lets games reach the controller directly (adaptive triggers and haptic feedback through Proton), so Games → This computer no longer says "missing udev rule" with no way to fix it: when games can't reach the controller, Set up USB access is right there, and the line is read again once it's done. All 7 languages.
- **"Needs attention" means one thing on Games.** The library's filter is now **Games that need setup**, and the settings panel is called **Games** like the rail, with a line saying what it changes (your launchers on this PC, nothing until you apply) instead of a status that disagreed with the filter's count; what waits for you still carries its yellow dot. All 7 languages.
- **The HDR checklist names the place to install our Proton.** It said "install it on the Proton card", a card that's gone; it now says Games → DualSense Proton build, the section's name. All 7 languages.
- **"Click any part of the drawing" sits right under the drawing.** It was below the tiles and data cards, off-screen in a normal window. Its line stays in place while a part is picked, so nothing under it jumps.
- **Games → Home opens on your games.** The Library now comes before This computer (the controller and HDR checks), which moved after it; its yellow dot and the links to it still find it. The list beside the page is one plain A–Z list (◆ marks a game with a profile) instead of Playing / With profile / All games groups, which the filters already do; the grid keeps your sort. In a small window the list is the library: the cover grid and its sort aren't shown there, the filters and Show still narrow the list.
- **A game's page: each fact once.** DualSense support (the tier, what works, what the tiers mean) is something to read, so it's now a block on the page itself, next to Details, instead of a section in the settings panel. Your star rating and the Feedback ticks are both your report on the game, so they're one section now, **Your report**. The panel's order is Controller profile, Setup, Compatibility, HDR, Your report, Notes, and the tiles at the top follow it with the same names (Controller profile, Setup, Compatibility, Your report); a tile gives the short value (how many changes, the Proton it runs with, your stars) and its section's line the detail (which settings change, what's recommended, your words for the rating), so the two never say the same thing. All 7 languages.
- **Every settings panel's second line says where its settings are kept.** Under the title: "On the Pico 2 W · pairing slot 0" on the Controller page, "This PC only · saved as you change them" on App settings, "Kept on this PC · a fix changes files only when you apply it" on a game's page, "Guide, changes and credits" on About. Versions left those lines (About's showed the app's version in the same spot where the Pico 2 W page showed the firmware's), and About's texts no longer repeat "You're running version …" on every page: the version is on the credits card. All 7 languages.
- **App settings shows your controller as a preview only.** Its main view is now the drawing with its color and status line, where a theme, accent or color change shows at once; the battery / signal tiles and the input, motion and connection cards (which no app setting changes) stay on the Controller page.
- **The Controller page says each thing once.** The Signal tile now carries the dB (−5 dB, or "ideal range") as its small line; the Connection card keeps only the link's updates and round trip; the headset jack and mute show only as the chips on the drawing ("Headset with mic in" when the headset has a microphone); the Battery tile also says "Fully charged"; the Player tile is the **Player indicator** without the pairing slot (it's in the panel's second line). Controller info is grouped: the firmware and hardware first, then **Power** (battery voltage, a charge fault, charging time, charge cycles and errors), then Lifetime and the button presses; the level and charging stay on the tile, and a newer official firmware is said once, in the block's header. All 7 languages.
- **Every section reads the same way: settings, then its live meter, then its test.** Adaptive triggers: Weaker by, then the Pull bars, then the Adaptive trigger test. Haptic feedback: the intensity, the audio buffer and Audio Auto Haptics, then the level meter, then the left / right / both buttons, now in their own **Haptic feedback test** group. Microphone: Microphone level and Echo cancellation moved above the Microphone test instead of inside it. All 7 languages.
- **The Pico 2 W page's panel starts with the OLED screen.** Sections in order of use, the danger zone last: **OLED screen**, **Power & sleep**, **Connection to the PC** (polling rate, controller mode, Reconnect USB, and Set up USB access, moved out of Restart & reset), **Status lights** (the Pico's status LED and the status pin, together now), **Firmware** (its yellow dot and the banner still say when an update waits), **Restart & reset**. The panel's second line says the settings are on your board for every pairing slot; the firmware version is in Firmware only. All 7 languages.
- **A section with nothing to do doesn't open.** When there's nothing to set or do right now (a game's Setup with no fix, HDR all set for a game we know, Compatibility already on our Proton with no other build, Games' Recommended changes with nothing to change, Change history with no change, our Proton installed and current, no dismissed notices), the section shows its line only, with no arrow and nothing to open; the line says how things stand. A game's Compatibility now offers **Install the DualSense Proton build** when a game needs it and it isn't installed, and takes you to Games → DualSense Proton build. All 7 languages.
- **One "Check for updates".** The Pico 2 W page's Firmware button said "Check now" while App settings said "Check for updates" for the same check; both say **Check for updates** now, and App settings → Updates has a **Firmware: Pico 2 W → Firmware** button that takes you to the board's firmware. All 7 languages.
- **"Read my game launchers" is in Games → Launchers.** The switch moved from App settings → Privacy to the Launchers section on Games → Home, the place it acts on; it still asks before turning off, and Privacy now says whether it's on with a button that takes you there. All 7 languages.
- **Smaller tidy-ups across the pages.** App settings: **Appearance** first, now with **HDR lighting** (an effect on the drawing), and **Hardware acceleration** moved to **Startup and window** (both ask for a restart), so the Graphics section is gone; Language lower down and without its repeated label; Background dim and blur show only with the **Game art** background, where they do something. Light bar: the favorite colors' hex codes are small print next to the swatch. A game's page: Details no longer repeats its store and size in its header, the Controller profile's chips leave out the button layout and stick curves (they're edited right below), and the button reads **Edit on the Controller page**. About: the text no longer repeats its section's name above it, Firmware changes shows its newest version like the others, and Credits lists its chapters instead of repeating the production line. All 7 languages.
- **One way to save: the bar at the bottom.** Button assignments, stick curves and calibration had their own Save / Apply / Revert buttons, and the PC sleep switches saved at once; now every board setting is kept the same way. Change anything and the bar says **Not saved yet**; **Save to the Pico 2 W** writes it all (buttons, curves, calibration, PC sleep and the settings), **Revert** puts all of it back. Folding a section or visiting another page keeps your unsaved changes. **Reset all** (buttons), **Back to Linear** (curves) and **Reset to uncalibrated** are changes like any other, kept by the bar; Reset to uncalibrated only shows when there's a calibration to undo. While a game's profile is on, the bar saves to the profile as before; calibration and the PC sleep options belong to your board and wait for its Save once the profile ends.
- **Calibration where its part is.** Trigger calibration moved into **Adaptive triggers** (before the Pull bars and the test), and gyroscope calibration into its own **Gyroscope** section after Sticks & calibration, which keeps the sticks' calibration, curves and tests; each part is measured on its own. The Sticks & calibration line says how they're set (calibrated or not, each stick's curve) instead of the pairing slot. All 7 languages.
- **Language is findable in every language.** App settings → Language shows the word in your current language as its title and in every other language right under it (Language · 语言 · Sprache · Idioma · Langue · 言語), always visible, with the 🌐 globe; so if you switch to a language you can't read, you can still find your way back. The section opens on the picker alone (each language in its own name). Screen readers hear it in the current language.
- **No hide button in the panel's header either.** The small panel button next to the ⋮ is gone on every page: the rail item of the page you're on shows and hides the panel, the one way everywhere (in a small window, Escape closes it too). All 7 languages.
- **No greyed-out buttons that can't do anything.** A button now shows only when it can act; otherwise the line says how things stand. **Set up USB access** shows "✓ Installed" once the rule is in place (Pico 2 W page, setup screen, Games → This computer). Also: **Test the voice** only with the narrator's voice on; My controller's colors' **From my colorway** only when a colorway is known and **Reset** only with colors to reset; **Back to Linear** only when a curve isn't Linear; calibration's **Start calibration** only with a controller connected (the hint says to connect one); a game's profile shows **Edit on the Controller page** and **Copy current settings** only with your board connected, **Create from current settings** only with it connected (else the hint), and its button-layout and curve pickers only when there's something to pick (the hint says why otherwise); the Developer section's reset only with a preview on. Switches that depend on the one above them (Audio Auto Haptics' strength, HDR lighting without hardware acceleration…) still show greyed while it's off, as they say what turning it on gives. All 7 languages.
